known_facts_book1: An island in the center of a lake a full mile from shore to shore, at the far northern edge of the Gillikin Country, bordering the desert and near the mountains of Oogaboo.
Is almost entirely covered by a huge round building with glass walls and a high glass dome, with only polished white marble between the building and the water's edge — no grass, flowers or shrubbery.
Contains under the dome a whole village of colored marble houses with stained-glass windows, streets, gardens and parks, lit at night by brilliant incandescent lamps.
**Rests on a base of solid marble** carried by a great steel pillar that runs from the basement up into the palace, whose hollowed upper end forms a basin in the Room of Magic.
Is raised and lowered by burning **Gaulau powder** in that basin and speaking one word, which expands or shortens the steel pillar — an art the Adepts had taught Coo-ee-oh as 'how to expand steel'.
The Dome does not leak and has been submerged several times before, though Coo-ee-oh disliked doing it because it takes a lot of hard work to operate the machinery.
Is left with no way out once submerged: no door or window opens, the basement doors need magic words, and the submarines obey only spoken commands.
Was built for the Skeezers by the **three Adepts**, along with their marble houses, back when the two peoples were friends.
Ends the book raised higher than before, because the lake had been drawn down; Glinda refills the lake and the Scarecrow replaces the removed pane.

known_facts_book1: An oblong hill towering above a flowery plain, with sides straight up and down like the wall of a house and a flat, level top.
Its top is shaped like a **saucer**, so that the rock houses and buildings inside cannot be seen from the plain below.

Is reached only by an entrance cut in the rock wall on the side facing the palm trees, leading to an **up-and-down stairway**: ten steps up, five steps down, then a turn — gaining only five steps a trip and forcing everyone to walk three times as far as necessary.
Rings a bell on the mountain top at every tenth step, warning the Flatheads of anyone coming; Ozma hears it from the first flight because she is holding her wand.
Is guarded by an **invisible wall** of stone and cement built a short distance in front of the entrance, with a gap at one end close to the mountainside just wide enough for one person.
The wall was made invisible on purpose: a visible wall would show strangers where to walk around it, and the Flatheads themselves need the gap to get out.
The wall was built **after the Adepts were transformed**, not before.
Holds at its center the palace of the Supreme Dictator, with a bronze prison for anyone he chooses to confine.
Is visited last, on the way home, so the Su-dic can be punished after the rescue rather than before.

known_facts_book1: Coo-ee-oh's whole system rests on **three magic words**, one to work the bridge, one to send out the submarines, one to raise and lower the island.
Hiding a spell behind a spoken word is a method **the Adepts themselves taught her**, which is why nobody else's magic can open the doors.
The three words are the three syllables of her own name — **Coo**, **ee**, **oh** — a guess made by Dorothy from the fact that both come in threes.
**'Coo'** sends every submarine loose out of its room and under water; **'ee'** extends the steel bridge joint by joint to the shore; **'Oh-h-h!'** raises the island.
Each word only works while a measure of **Gaulau** — a rare grayish mineral powder whose tiny grains constantly move as if alive — is burning in the basin atop the steel pillar.
The powder is kept in a hidden drawer that pops out of the wall of the Room of Magic when a thumb is pressed into a slight hollow, with a tiny golden measuring cup inside.
Glinda recognises Gaulau as known to sorcerers and more wonderful than radium, and wonders where Coo-ee-oh ever obtained it.
The marble basement door is a separate problem: it was commanded to open only to its one word, so **no other magic word has any effect on it at all** — which is why Glinda's sorcery cannot force it.

known_facts_book1: Several enclosed boats of blackened steel kept in little rooms in the basement of the island, each room with two doors — one to the basement, one to the lake.
Have a collapsible roof that rises from the sides and joins overhead into a water-tight chamber with four glass windows, one on each side and one at either end.
Are **not operated by machinery but by mystic words** spoken by Coo-ee-oh, which is why her own crew is left helpless the moment she is transformed.
Have no oars, no sails and no motive power of any kind.
Are launched by opening the basement door, closing it, then slowly opening the outer door to flood the room and float the boat out under water; a pump empties the room again for the return.
One is left stranded and empty on the beach after Coo-ee-oh's defeat, and drifts there while three Skeezers wait beside it for three days.
Are made to obey **sorcery instead of witchcraft** by Glinda, using magic recipe No. 1163 with the Wizard's skeropythrope, a powder and a vial of liquid, in a shower of violet sparks.

known_facts_book1: The **Magic Belt** was taken from the Nome King and is worn by Dorothy around her waist; it protects her from harm and makes the Spider King unable even to touch her.
The **Magic Ring** is Glinda's, given to Dorothy at the start with instructions to turn it once right and once left only if she is in actual danger of destruction.
Turning the ring rings the great alarm bell in Glinda's palace, and that bell is the sole reason the Rescue Expedition exists.
The ring conveys no other message: Glinda has to go to her magic room to learn what the danger is, and the answer is only that the two are prisoners under the lake.
The **Silver Wand** is Ozma's, tipped with a great sparkling emerald, slipped into the bosom of her gown; fairies use no chemicals, herbs or wizards' tools.

The wand is Ozma's one weapon of offence and defence: it conjures the Magic Tent and its meals, renders her and Dorothy invisible, lights the dark stairway with green-tinted light, lets her hear sounds a great distance off, changes the crab's color and draws the silence-circle around Lady Aurex's house.
**None of the three can raise the island**, which is the point: Dorothy's Belt, Glinda's ring and Ozma's wand together leave them still prisoners under the water.

known_facts_book1: Glinda's greatest treasure, prized above all her magical possessions, lying open on a big marble table in her palace court.
Is firmly attached to the table by **golden chains**, and whenever Glinda leaves home she locks it with **five jeweled padlocks** and carries the keys hidden in her bosom.
Prints a record of every event that happens in any part of the world at exactly the moment it happens, and the records are always truthful — though brief, since so many things happen.
Records little about the Land of Oz, which is usually peaceful and uneventful.
Prints the notice of the Skeezer–Flathead war **while Dorothy is looking at the page**, which is how the whole book begins.
Is consulted by Glinda every day, and tells her of Ozma's arrival at the mountain, the escape, the submerging of the island and the Queen's transformation into a swan.

**Its usefulness ends when Glinda leaves home**: Ervic's rescue of the three fishes is recorded in the Book after she has set out, so she knows nothing of it and searches the lake for fishes already gone.
